messages:
laura: Noticed a jump in bundle re-downloads + slow initial chart paints after yesterday's quota change. p75 payload size +18kb for widgets.

rishi: Which quota change? the routing quota or api ingress token limit?

laura: The routing quota tweak (reduced per-route concurrent inflight from 200->120) plus a small CDN TTL change.

anya: Telemetry: increased bundle GETs around the same time as the quota change. Many clients show `304` then immediate full re-fetch afterwards. Could be cache-on-error behavior when prefetch gets rate-limited.

noah: We pushed `client-prefetch` v1.4 last week which treats 429s as cache-bypass. If the router returns 429 due to lower concurrency, the client re-downloads assets.

ux: Users in APAC are seeing UI jank on big dashboards (heatmaps + sparklines). UX report attached to the incident playbook.

deploy-bot: config change routing.quota/2026-03-20 by rishi applied at 2026-03-20T15:02:03Z.

rishi: Oof. So the combo is: lower inflight -> some prefetches get 429 -> client marks bundle as invalid and re-downloads -> CDN TTL low so downloads hit origin -> origin throttles -> main thread stall.

laura: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) bump routing inflight back to 200 for the next 2h; 2) temporarily treat 429 in client prefetch as retryable (exponential backoff) not cache-bypass; 3) raise CDN TTL for JS assets to 10m.

anya: Also add an observability check: prefetch 429 rate and bundle re-download count per client-ip. Make it a canary gate for future quota changes.

noah: I can ship client fix as a runtime flag so we don't need a full client deploy: `prefetch.on_429 = backoff` via remote config.

rishi: I'll roll routing quota to 200 for 2h now. Command: `/config set routing.inflight_per_route 200 --ttl 2h --reason "investigating bundle churn"`

deploy-bot: config update scheduled by rishi at 2026-03-21T00:12:10Z.

laura: Obs, please create temporary dashboard: metrics: `bundle.redownloads`, `prefetch.429_rate`, `mainthread.lcp_ms`, `bundle.size.bytes`. Throw an alert if redownloads > 50/min.

observability-bot: Dashboard `/dashboards/bundle-churn-6166000001` created. Alert rule `bundle.redownloads > 50/min` configured.

noah: Flagging a long-term require: client should include `x-routing-session` header and server should avoid returning pool-specific identifiers in cache keys (we currently include `pool-id` in asset URLs for affinity). That causes revalidation mismatches when routed to different pools.

anya: Agree. Also, add a soft per-client prefetch concurrency cap (e.g. 6) enforced at the router to avoid flood when clients retry.

rishi: For the rollback step: rolling the `inflight_per_route` back to 200 now. Monitoring.

laura: After the config change, I'm already seeing bundle redownloads dropping. Nice. Keep monitoring for 30m.

observability-bot: Alert triggered at 2026-03-21T00:18:00Z: bundle.redownloads 120/min -> paging muted by laura.

observability-bot: Alert resolved at 2026-03-21T00:42:00Z (redownloads back to baseline).

ux: UX notes: once engineering stabilizes, we'll run a small canary with heavy dashboards in EU/APAC before we change routing again. Also propose a visible rollout banner for internal customers so support teams can triage layout regressions.

laura: Good plan. I'll open the RFC for: 1) remove `pool-id` from asset cache keys; 2) add `x-routing-session` header; 3) canary gating on `prefetch.429_rate` + `bundle.redownloads`. Assigning owners: anya (cache-key), noah (client side), rishi (router gating).

noah: I'll also add an integration test that simulates route churn and verifies client does not invalidate bundles on 429.

laura: Closing for now. Follow-up doc in #postmortems with timeline and CI for regression tests. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
